national_context: STRONGEST EVIDENCE: real NFLIS-Drug California forensic-lab counts (data/raw/ground_truth/nflis_ca_counts.csv) show xylazine substantial statewide (n=24-61 per half-year) by 2019-2020 -- a ~4.5-year lag before LA's own ME-death onset (2023Q3), roughly triple the ~2-quarter estimate this cell used to carry. That earlier estimate wasn't wrong, it was answering a narrower question: LA's own drug-checking data shows xylazine was still undetectable in LA's fentanyl supply as of 2023Q1, so the ~2-quarter figure is the lag from 'present in LA's supply' to 'showing up in LA deaths' -- a real, but much shorter, second stage of a longer statewide-to-local diffusion. LA County DPH's own 2023-03-08 alert cited zero LA-specific detection data (see health_notices.csv) -- consistent with this. See docs/findings/ground_truth.md for the full comparison.

This is LA's defining local overdose epidemic -- included as the largest and most obvious real emergence in the dataset, not because it needed a subtle rule to find.

The correct reading of the rise is 'the fentanyl supply is being cut differently,' not 'lidocaine is killing people.' interval_start/interval_end are a placeholder (its peak alarm quarter) purely so this row parses; no_emergence=True means `score` ignores them.
